div.head: II Ew II Ew. 1
div.ab: Eadweard cyning myngode his wytan, þa hy æt Exanceastre wæron, þæt hy smeadon ealle, hu heora frið betere beon mæhte, þonne hit ær ðam wæs; forðam him þuhte, þæt hit mæctor gelæst wære, þonne hit scolde, þæt he ær beboden hæfde.

Eadweard cyning mid his witan, ða hy æt Exceastre wæron, smeadon ealle, hu heora frið betere beon mehte, ðone hit ær ðam wæs; forðam him ðuhte, þæt hit mæctor gelæst wære, ðonne hit scolde, þæt he ær beboden hæfde.

Eadwardus rex admonuit omnes sapientes suos, quando fuerunt Exonie, ut inuestigarent simul et quererent, quomodo pax eorum melior esse posset, quam antea fuit; quia uisum est ei, quod hoc mediocrius impletum sit, quam deceret, et quam antea precepisset.

[Be fryþe.] Eadweard cyning myngode his wytan, þa hy æt Exanceastre wæron, þæt hy smeadon ealle, hu heora frið betere beon mæhte, þonne hit ær ðam wæs; forðam him þuhte, þæt hit mæctor gelæst wære, þonne hit scolde, þæt he ær beboden hæfde.

(Von öffentlicher Sicherheit. Ld) König Eadward ermahnte seine Witan, als sie zu Exeter waren, dass sie alle berathschlagen möchten, wie ihre öffentliche Sicherheit besser werden könne, als es vordem war; denn ihm schien, dass jenes, was er früher geboten hatte, minder, als es sich gebührte, erfüllt wäre.

(Of public security. Ld) King Edward exhorted his witan, when they were at Exeter, that they should all deliberate how their public security might become better than it was before; for it seemed to him that what he had commanded earlier was fulfilled less than was fitting.

King Edward exhorted all his councillors, when they were at Exeter, to consider how the public peace for which they were responsible could be kept better than it had been, because it seemed to him that his previous orders had not been carried out so well as they ought to have been.

‘Landfrieden’ geht an, darf aber nicht (Price) mit späteren Deutschen Landfriedensverträgen zusammengebracht werden. Unter ‘ihr’ kann 1. ‘König und Witan’ allein oder 2. ‘samt Volk’ gemeint sein, und sowohl 3. die genossene Ruhe und Ordnung wie auch 4. der von jenen ausgehende (gewährleistete) Schutz. Mir scheint der Zusammenhang zu deuten auf nur aristokratische Machtübung (vgl. Gl Frieden 4) zugunsten auch demokratischen Vorteils der Regierten

‘Landfrieden’ will do, but must not be connected (as by Price) with the later German Landfrieden compacts. By ‘their’ may be meant 1. ‘king and witan’ alone or 2. ‘together with the people’, and both 3. the peace and order enjoyed and 4. the protection proceeding (guaranteed) from them. The context seems to me to point to a purely aristocratic exercise of power (cf. Gl Frieden 4) that was also to the democratic advantage of the governed
